knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: 3.2.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. Which statement correctly describes forming a confidence interval from a given sampling distribution?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: The move is to invert a known sampling/pivotal relationship. Memorised Normal-mean recipes do not replace using the distribution you were actually given.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Invert the given sampling distribution / pivot to isolate the parameter.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Jumping to a Normal-mean template instead of inverting the given law.

choices.label: Given a sampling distribution for an estimator or pivotal quantity, invert that distributional relationship to isolate the parameter and obtain a confidence interval.
Always use the Normal-mean cookbook formula x̄ ± z s/√n, regardless of the sampling distribution you are given.
A given sampling distribution is used only to simulate data; the interval endpoints are chosen by eye from a histogram.
If a sampling distribution is given, the confidence interval is the support of that distribution with no inversion step.

knowledge_checks.title: Checkpoint: 3.2.3
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. For an Exponential mean-θ model you are told that 2n X̄ / θ ~ χ²_{2n}. Which statement is correct?
knowledge_checks.body: Invert the given chi-square pivot; refuse Normal-cookbook-as-done.
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: From χ²_L < 2n X̄ / θ < χ²_U, taking reciprocals (and reversing inequalities) yields bounds 2n X̄ / χ²_U and 2n X̄ / χ²_L. The given pivot must be used; Normal-mean cookbooks are not a substitute.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Invert P(χ²_L < 2n X̄ / θ < χ²_U)=1−α to bounds in 2n X̄ / χ²; refuse Normal-mean template.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Ignoring the given χ² pivot or inverting the inequality incorrectly.

choices.label: Choose χ² critical values so P(χ²_L < 2n X̄ / θ < χ²_U) = 1−α, then rearrange to isolate θ (bounds involve 2n X̄ / χ²). A memorised Normal-mean CI formula does not replace that inversion for this model.
Because X̄ is approximately Normal for large n, ignore the given χ² relationship and always use x̄ ± z s/√n for θ.
The interval for θ is (χ²_L, χ²_U) with no dependence on X̄, because the pivot already contains all information.
Rearrange to θ ∈ (2n X̄ · χ²_L, 2n X̄ · χ²_U), multiplying by the critical values instead of dividing.

worked_example.title: CI from a stated Normal sampling distribution
worked_example.problem_statement: An estimator θ̂ of a portfolio proportion satisfies θ̂ ~ N(θ, 0.01²) exactly (sampling distribution given). Observing θ̂ = 0.42, construct a 95% confidence interval for θ.
worked_example.attempt_before_reveal: CMP closed. Invert θ̂ ~ N(θ, 0.01²) into θ̂ ± 1.96 × 0.01.

steps.label: Identify the pivot half-width
steps.explanation: When the sampling distribution is given as Normal with known SD, the CI is the estimate plus/minus z times that SD.

worked_example.common_pitfall: Dividing 0.01 by √n when no sample size is part of the given sampling distribution, or using 0.42 ± 1.96 × 0.01².
